observations.fatal_message: stalled RAW timeout epoch=2 consumer=7 parent=6

classification.root_cause: The TB turns every transient stalled_same_address event into a forward-only eight-cycle obligation. The RTL predicate can fire while sink readiness is low and has no reserved-count condition, whereas a forward requires reserved_count<2. A prior response may fill the queue before the live write, so the consumer is legally delivered later by macro read/response instead of forward. The TB token is never cleared by that exact alternative path or by consumer completion. No eight-cycle sink fairness contract exists.
classification.unit_delay_phase_assessment: The foundry UNIT_DELAY model updates Q 10 ps after the read edge; top r2 consumes the response on the following edge. The negedge identity/data checker did not fail, so the logged failure is not evidence of a macro response-phase mismatch.

decision.allowed_candidate: TB-only r5 repair of the causal RAW monitor; no RTL/top/macro/SVA datapath edit
required_repair: Track exact parent delivery by either matching forward or matching macro read response; do not equate delivery with forward only.
Remove the unconditional eight wall-clock cycle fatal unless an explicit bounded sink-fairness premise is added and driven.
Keep direct stalled-RAW-to-forward as an independent required cover; the sealed r11 SVA already reports six matches before the fatal.
Add observation-only trace fields for raw token identity, current row, slot0/slot1 identities, pending identity, reserved count, sink readiness, forward, macro-read, and read-response.
Keep all cleanroom arithmetic, queue/data identity, conservation, attack, fatal/error, and PASS-token gates unchanged.
forbidden: extend timeout without a fairness proof
edit top r2 to satisfy the false monitor
disable or remove response identity checks
count a request as delivered before the matching response

p0.finding: C1 remains not RTL verified because r11 has no functional PASS token; repair and re-release the TB-only causal monitor before one new VCS candidate.
